Status: Backlog (backlog)

## Problem

No ticket tests whether a quest-selection director beats random quest choice on the same seeds. Yu, Guzdial and Sturtevant (AIIDE 2024, DOI 10.1609/aiide.v20i1.31885) report that, in a human-subject study on a different test bed (FarmQuest), a non-random AI director gave better player experience than random selection. That result came from their setting, not HBL's. Here it is a hypothesis to test.

## Player story

When the game offers my next quest, it fits what I just did, not a random pick.

## Scientific justification

A director result is only meaningful next to a random baseline run on the same seeds.

## Scope

4. Null check: two random policies with different labels should show no systematic difference.

## Out of scope

* New quest content.
* Any claim about fun before the paired results are posted.
* Player surveys. These need a separate consent ticket.

## Acceptance criteria

* Metric list and stop rule committed to the repo before the first run.
* Paired results reported with effect size and an interval.
* Null check result reported.
* A note listing what was not measured.

Linear issue SHE-219: [HBL-RES-08] 1M feasibility E2: show that residents really interact, with an interaction-ablation test

Status: Done (completed)
URL: https://linear.app/shel-bernstein/issue/SHE-219/hbl-res-08-1m-feasibility-e2-show-that-residents-really-interact-with

**Source:** `docs/research/million-agent-architectures.md`, experiment E2. Not covered by [SHE-141](https://linear.app/shel-bernstein/issue/SHE-141/hbl-1m-014-define-the-operational-meaning-of-1-million-interacting)–153, [SHE-171](https://linear.app/shel-bernstein/issue/SHE-171/hbl-1m-044-build-a-reproducible-headless-million-agent-benchmark), [SHE-177](https://linear.app/shel-bernstein/issue/SHE-177/hbl-1m-050-define-a-verified-release-gate-for-the-million-resident) or [SHE-191](https://linear.app/shel-bernstein/issue/SHE-191/build-the-simulation-benchmark-arena).

## Why

Updating a million records independently is easy. The claim worth making is that residents *interact*. [SHE-141](https://linear.app/shel-bernstein/issue/SHE-141/hbl-1m-014-define-the-operational-meaning-of-1-million-interacting) checks that individual interaction events change state; this test checks that interaction matters at the outcome level.

## Method

Use the same seeds and population in five arms:

1. full coupling (current rules);
2. no interaction — each agent sees frozen or independent copies of shared resources, and has no partners;
3. shuffled partners and resources (same counts, random assignment);
4. coupling × 0.5;
5. coupling × 2.

Measure:

* headline outcomes: commute time, employment, occupancy and rent;
* interaction-graph statistics: mean degree, giant-component share and cross-shard share.

Start at 10k and 100k people with the existing population model (the `world/PEOPLE_BENCHMARK.md` route). Reuse the [SHE-171](https://linear.app/shel-bernstein/issue/SHE-171/hbl-1m-044-build-a-reproducible-headless-million-agent-benchmark) runner once it exists.

## Pass

Full coupling and no interaction differ beyond the 95% seed band on at least two headline outcomes, with the number of seeds stated. If they don't, the product must not claim "interacting residents" at that fidelity.

## Player story

When a neighbor mentions the drainage change, I can trace who told whom, and when it started.

## Scientific justification

Axelrod (1997, DOI 10.1177/0022002797041002001) shows that local convergence can produce global polarization in a cultural dissemination model. A v0 run shows whether HBL's own rules do this, measured against a control.

1. One idea type, for example "the drainage policy changed".

## Out of scope

* Player-facing narrative text.
* Claims about real-world information spread.
* Performance at one million residents.

## Acceptance criteria

* Same seed gives the same spread (deterministic replay).
* For each informed resident, the provenance chain reaches the origin.
* Spread curve compared with the no-sharing control, and the comparison reported.
* Agent-count contract in world/metrics/agent-counts.js still holds.

* behavior after the tab is backgrounded and restored;

* T3 and T4 do not run out of memory at the claimed population.
* Each tier has a documented fallback: a lower population, lower fidelity, or a different renderer.

The stages:

1. A research issue states the question, hypothesis, data sources, intended use and acceptance criteria.
2. Symphony sends the issue to a Codex research worker, which implements model changes, data adapters, experiments and tests.

* Research gate: the scientific claims are credible.

Linear issue SHE-213: [HBL-REV-05] WebKit-safe flagship demo: stop per-month URL writes and add a WebKit test lane
Repository: adnanwahab/happybearlandia
Base: sprint/one-city-two-futures-20261111
Status: Done (completed)
URL: https://linear.app/shel-bernstein/issue/SHE-213/hbl-rev-05-webkit-safe-flagship-demo-stop-per-month-url-writes-and-add

**Source:** `docs/reviews/claude.md`, finding F1 and improvement I1. This is a static finding based on a documented browser limit; it has not yet been reproduced on a device. It matters most for iPhone demos.

## Problem

* `world/future-machine/main.js` `setMonth()` calls `updateURL()`, which calls `history.replaceState`, on every month change.
* The guided demo moves through all 121 months between 4 s and 38 s, and Play timelapse writes every 200 ms.
* WebKit throws `SecurityError` after 100 calls per 30 s. Firefox throws at a higher limit; Chromium silently drops the extra calls.
* `setMonth()` catches the exception into `state.error` after `stage.update()` but before the inspector refresh. The result is an alert banner near Month \~110 of the demo, a stale WHY panel, and a share URL that no longer matches the month.
* The banner stays up: a successful `setMonth()` never clears `state.error`.
* All browser evidence so far comes from Chromium.

## Change

* Write the URL only on pause, stop, share or a manual seek, or debounce it to at least 350 ms. Compute the share URL when it is requested.
* Add Playwright WebKit and Firefox to the canonical journey.
* Add an init script to Chromium runs that emulates WebKit's limit: throw after 100 `replaceState`/`pushState` calls per 30 s.
* In explicit `?renderer=canvas2d` mode, don't import Three or OrbitControls at all.

## Acceptance

* The canonical journey (homepage → Play Demo → first divergence → timeline → outcomes → WHY) passes on Playwright WebKit with 0 page errors, and after pausing, the URL `month` equals `state.month`.
* The full demo and a 0→120 timelapse pass in Chromium with the emulation script.
* In Canvas mode, the network log shows no `/vendor/three/` request.
* One run on a physical iPhone is recorded before anyone claims mobile support.

**Dispatch:** Backlog. `main.js` is coordinator-owned. Not approved for Symphony.

**Verdict:** D01 MODIFY (S). **Source:** `docs/reviews/claude.md` § D01, findings F2–F4.

## Problem

* **Three production rules pick the "first divergence":**
  * `main.js` `physicalStop()`, used by the demo;
  * `scene/effects.js` `firstPhysicalStop()`, which is unit-tested but unused in production;
  * `story/index.js` `buildStory()`, used by "Show Me What Changed".

  They agree for seed 42, but can disagree when two buildings diverge in the same month.
* **20 Hz UI rebuilds.** The director ticks every 50 ms, and every tick runs a full `ui.update()` for 50 s, rebuilding the household `<select>` options each time.
* **Screen-reader chatter.** `.fm-demo-caption` has `role=status` and appends a seconds counter, so it is announced every second.
* **Lost selection.** A building clicked while `playDemo()` is waiting on `run()`/`whenReady()` gets overwritten, because `select()` does not bump `demoGeneration`.
* **Skipped hold.** A hidden tab can skip the Month-16 hold, because elapsed time is measured by wall clock.

2. Emit `onState` only when the caption, status or whole second changes, and coalesce `update()` per animation frame.
3. Keep the seconds counter out of the live region.
4. Pause the director on `visibilitychange`.
5. Have `select()` increment `demoGeneration`.

## Acceptance

* During the demo, a MutationObserver records 0 mutations of the household `<select>` children while the month is unchanged.
* The live region changes only when the caption changes (6 times or fewer per demo).
* Unit test: hide the tab at 9 s and show it at 30 s; the director resumes inside the Month-16 hold.
* Clicking a building while `whenReady()` is pending keeps that selection, and the demo does not start.
* `firstDivergence()` returns Month 16 / `building-project-policy-1-0` for seed 42, and grep finds no other implementation.

**Verdict:** D03 MODIFY, renderer only (M). Keep the model contract: `construction-progress.js` and layout v2 are exemplary. **Source:** `docs/reviews/claude.md` § D03, finding F2.

## Problem

* `scene/index.js` `rebuild()` disposes and recreates every mesh, material, edge geometry and progress gauge on every `update`, `focus` and `setMode`.

* `canvas-stage.js` `getStats()` reports `future-machine-layout.v1` while the mapping is v2.

## Change

* Keep a retained mesh map keyed `arm:collection:id:ghost`. Create a mesh when an entity appears, update its material and height in place, and dispose it when the entity disappears.
* Diff the label layer instead of calling `replaceChildren()`.
* Fix the Canvas layout-version constant.
* Optional: show the recorded `TOPPED_OUT` event in WHY. Do not draw invented intermediate floors.

## Acceptance

* After a second full 0→120 scrub, `renderer.info.memory.geometries` equals its value after the first.
* With playback paused and the camera still, draw calls drop to 0 within 1 s.
* Scrubbing 16→15 removes the building in the same frame, and 15→16 shows its full recorded floors.
* `canvasStage.getStats().layoutVersion === LAYOUT_VERSION`.

* When graphics arrive, the month, selection and camera fit are unchanged.
* With Three blocked entirely, the existing all-contexts-unavailable behavior (R07) still holds.

Linear issue SHE-222: [HBL-DEF-06] Quick win: Mechanism Microscope — split the mean-rent delta into price change and composition
Repository: adnanwahab/happybearlandia
Base: sprint/one-city-two-futures-20261111
Status: Done (completed)
URL: https://linear.app/shel-bernstein/issue/SHE-222/hbl-def-06-quick-win-mechanism-microscope-split-the-mean-rent-delta

**Source:** `docs/research/shared-simulation-capabilities.md`, idea #19. This directly addresses the sprint's own caveat that mean rent includes new inventory (`docs/one-city-two-futures-sprint.md`).

## Experience

In the rent card's WHY panel, a stacked bar splits the Month-120 delta (−740.769 USD/month for seed 42) into two parts:

* the change in existing units' rents;
* the composition effect of the 24 new units.

## Method

Use the exact shift-share identity, with `cityMetrics`' own `meanRent` definition and denominator:

Δ = (mean of existing units in the plan − baseline mean) + w_new × (mean of new units − mean of existing units in the plan)

where w_new is the new units' share. New units are identified with `housingProjectBuildingId()`.

## Acceptance

* The two components sum to the recorded delta within 1e-6.
* Unit counts and the denominator are shown.
* It works at every month; at Month 0 both components are 0.

**Effort:** about a day. No model change.

**Dispatch:** Backlog. Product exploration outside the frozen sprint.

## Problem

A prediction score currently measures only how far a forecast is from the realised value. It does not compare the forecast with doing nothing. If a forecast that predicts no change scores well on some metrics, the score cannot show skill.

## Player story

When my prediction scores well, it means I beat the simple "nothing changes" guess, not just that I landed near a trend.

## Scientific and business justification

A skill score needs a baseline. Without one, a learning game can reward guessing trends.

## Current implementation evidence

* `world/learning/prediction.js` (229 lines) computes `score = max(0, 100 * (1 - absoluteError / tolerance))`.
* The score compares the forecast only with the realised change.
* The no-change value appears only as a baseline inside `resolvePrediction`.
* Tolerances: meanRent 250; meanCommuteMinutes, unemploymentRate, unhoused and housingUnits 10 each.
* `test/prediction-league.test.js` covers the league.

## Scope

1. Compute the error of the no-change forecast for each metric.
2. Store `noChangeError` and a skill value, `1 - error / noChangeError`, on resolved records.
3. Keep existing records readable. Add fields. Do not rewrite history.

## Out of scope

* Changing tolerances.
* Rescoring old predictions.
* UI changes beyond showing the new value.

## Acceptance criteria

* New resolved predictions include `noChangeError` and the skill value.
* Old records still load.
* Tests cover: a forecast equal to no-change has skill 0; a perfect forecast has skill 1; a zero no-change error does not divide by zero.

## Validation

* `bun test test/prediction-league.test.js`
* One example resolved record in the pull request.

## Metrics

* Share of resolved predictions with the skill value.
* Distribution of skill values, reported as information only. It is not evidence that the game works.

## Dependencies

* Related to [SHE-184](https://linear.app/shel-bernstein/issue/SHE-184/build-the-experiment-registry) (experiment registry) if prediction records are registered there.

## Risks

* Zero no-change error when nothing changes. Handle it explicitly.
